title: El Tiny Is Back! Latin Music Stars Take Over NPR's Tiny Desk
summary: What if your favorite music stars performed at a tiny desk — like, a real office desk — instead of a giant stage? That's exactly what NPR's Tiny Desk concerts are. And every year, for Hispanic Heritage Month, the desk gets a new name: El Tiny. From September 15 to October 15, El Tiny celebrates Latin American and Latino artists. The 2026 lineup was just announced, and it's packed. Los Tigres del Norte, Mon Laferte, Draco Rosa, Yendry, and many more will perform. "Since 2021, NPR's El Tiny concert series has brought the best of Latin music to new audiences," said Felix Contreras, co-host of Alt.Latino and co-producer of El Tiny. He added that Latin music is "the world's music." The Tiny Desk series has a history of spotlighting Latin talent. Stars like Bad Bunny, Karol G, and Grupo Frontera have all performed behind the desk. One set by Ca7riel and Paco Amoroso from 2024 has 55 million views on YouTube. That's a lot of eyeballs! This year's lineup includes Mon Laferte, Los Mirlos, Yendry, Alex Ferreira, Melissa Aldana and Gonzalo Rubalcaba, Panteón Rocóco, Tim Bernardes, Los Texmaniacs, Draco Rosa, and Los Tigres del Norte. Dates are still to come. Anamaria Sayre, co-host of Alt.Latino, said, "Whether you're a devoted fan or discovering these artists for the first time, there's something special about hearing them on the intimate Tiny Desk stage." So keep an eye out — your next favorite song might come from a tiny desk.
why_it_matters: A song from a small desk stage can end up on your own playlist, and it shows how music from another culture can become part of your everyday life.

background_read: NPR (National Public Radio) is a group of radio stations in the United States that also shares its shows and concerts online for free.
Tiny Desk concerts began when a musician played a song at a real desk in NPR's office, and the small idea grew into a famous series.

Hispanic Heritage Month is a time in the U.S. to celebrate people with roots in Latin America and Spain. Latin music has become some of the most popular music in the world, even in places where most people do not speak Spanish.
Article_Structure: WHO: NPR's Tiny Desk team, co-hosts Felix Contreras and Anamaria Sayre, and Latin stars like Los Tigres del Norte, Mon Laferte and Draco Rosa.
WHAT: NPR announced the 2026 El Tiny lineup — the list of Latin artists who will perform behind the Tiny Desk.
WHERE: At NPR's offices, with the sets shared online — one 2024 performance has 55 million views on YouTube.
WHY: El Tiny celebrates Hispanic Heritage Month and brings Latin music, 'the world's music,' to new audiences.

perspectives.description: They are excited because big names like Los Tigres del Norte and Mon Laferte get a global stage that even more people will see.
People who have never heard Latin music can discover it in a friendly, small setting — Sayre says there is something special about hearing artists on the intimate Tiny Desk stage.
